Subject: Billing math for long-context calls and minimums

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightCart liked the latency numbers. Two follow-ups from our finance team before we move to a PO:

1) We need a simple worked example that shows billing for a typical flow we run: 20k user prompts / month, average prompt 120 tokens, each generates ~600 tokens of model output because we do verbose extraction. We also interleave system prompts and maintain a 16k context window for about 40% of calls.
2) How do you apply the minimum billing/windowing? Do you round up per-call to a 1k token floor, or do you aggregate across session prefixes? We saw different behaviors in other vendors and need to reconcile with our forecasting.
3) If we commit to a quarterly reserved capacity, what floor/discount tradeoffs are available — specifically can you waive session minimums for committed volume?

Can you produce a short spreadsheet (sample math) and a one-paragraph summary of the rounding rules we can share with Finance?

Appreciate it — Charles
Director of Engineering
BrightCart

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Charles Nguyen <charles@brightcart.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightcart.com>

Subject: Re: Billing math for long-context calls and minimums

Hi Charles — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise spreadsheet (billing_examples.xlsx) with three scenarios, and a short summary below. TL;DR: we meter at the per-request token level, but we apply two levers that affect the invoice number: a per-request quantum (default 256 tokens) for rounding, and a session aggregation option (committed customers can enable per-session rollup which aggregates requests that share a prefix within a rolling 24-hour window).

Summary (one paragraph): Redwood charges per-token for both prompt and completion tokens. By default tokens are rounded up to the next 256-token quantum per request for metering (so a 120-token prompt + 600-token completion would be counted as two quanta: one for the prompt rounded to 256 and one for the completion rounded to 768 -> aggregated to 1024 tokens for that call). For customers on Reserved Capacity we can enable session rollup: requests that share a persisted prefix or KV cache within a 24-hour window are aggregated before applying the quantum, which reduces redundant rounding; session rollup also allows applying a lower quantum (128 tokens) as a committed benefit. We also include automatic KV/prefix caching credits for repeated tokens within the same session.

I'm happy to walk through the spreadsheet on call — if you want the committed pricing options called out next to the math, say the preferred commit level (monthly/quarterly) and I will add the discount rows.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Team — looping you in. Customer (BrightCart) asked whether we can waive/adjust per-request quantum rounding if they commit to a quarterly reserved capacity (they're targeting 20k calls/month with heavy long-context usage). Quick asks:

- Finance: what's the earliest acceptable minimum/quantum we can offer at 10k/mo, 30k/mo, and 60k/mo commits?
- Product: confirm session rollup can be enabled for a single account with 24-hour rolling aggregation, and whether KV-prefetch credits can be quantified as token discounts.
- Sales: recommended concession band we can offer without approval (e.g., reduce quantum from 256->128 and 5% discount) vs. escalations needed.

If you can send back bullet answers, I'll draft a short amendment to SOW_v1.pdf.

Thanks — Mateo

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-30T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing math for long-context calls and minimums — commit-level ask

Mateo — quick replies:

- Finance (high level): Approvals for standard AE concessions: up to 7% list discount and one-tier quantum reduction (256->192) for up to Q commitment without legal signoff. Anything beyond that (e.g., 128 quantum or >10% discount) needs Revenue Ops + legal.
- Product: Session rollup for a single account with 24-hour aggregation is supported; it collapses contiguous requests that share an active prefix/KV cache. Quantifying KV credits depends on access patterns; typical customers see ~8-12% token savings on long-lived sessions; we can estimate per BrightCart workload in the spreadsheet if they share a sample trace.
- Recommendation: Offer a pilot committed quarterly SKU: 30k/mo commit -> quantum reduced to 192 + 6% discount, and enable session rollup. That should materially reduce their rounding leakage and fits standard concession band.

Kim
Director, Finance Pricing

Charles — attaching an updated spreadsheet and a redline to the SOW (SOW_v1.pdf) with one optional committed SKU. Summary of the offer:

- Scenario used: 20k calls/month, avg prompt 120 tokens, avg completion 600 tokens; 40% of calls hold a 16k context window and reuse prefixes.
- Default (no commit): per-request metering with 256-token quantum, estimated monthly bill ~ 20k * (rounding per-call => see Sheet A) -> $X (cell formula in sheet).
- Committed Pilot SKU (quarterly, 30k/mo commit): quantum reduced to 192 tokens for metering, session rollup enabled (24-hour), and 6% committed discount. Using the same traffic profile, the estimated monthly bill reduces ~14% vs default (sheet B), primarily from lower rounding leakage and KV reuse credits.
- We will enable a 30-day pilot window where we apply session rollup and collect metrics; if you like the results we convert to a quarterly Reserved Capacity contract.

Next steps: If Procurement is OK with the pilot language I attached, we can generate a PO and start the pilot within 7 business days. Let me know if you want a short call (15m) to walk through line-by-line.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
